title: Away mode
summary: Say -away and the agent asks all its questions first, then finishes the whole task without you, with an optional usage stop point.
benefit: You can leave: Claude asks everything up front, then finishes the task on its own.
solves: Long tasks stop and wait for an answer while you are away from your desk.
use_cases: "-away" on any message: one round of questions now, then it never asks or waits; later dialogs are blocked.
"-back" ends it. Any other message you send is answered or followed, and the work goes on.
"-away 85": also stops cleanly when your weekly usage reaches 85%.
Usage limit hit while you are away: it waits for the reset and continues by itself.
"-away -p": you approve the plan before you leave.
Push, merge, deploy, production DB changes and messages to people stay undone unless the task asked.
details: When you add -away to a message (or -away 85 for a weekly usage stop point), Claude asks all its questions in one round first, then finishes the whole task without you, stopping at that usage level if set. It stays on until you write -back (or 72 hours pass), so a question in the middle does not end it. It is for leaving your desk mid task and still wanting the work done. It adds hooks that run on every prompt, tool call and stop, settings entries, a rule file loaded every session and an away-mode skill loaded only when used; the hooks run locally and use no network.
trigger: Add -away (or -away 85 for a weekly usage stop point) to your message; -back ends it.

values.ask: Extra tools still allowed after the stop point, as a JSON array of regexes such as ["mcp__<server>__.+"] (leave empty for none)

risk: Hooks run on every prompt, tool call and stop, and a skill holds the full rules; no network.
